title: Identity and cocycle laws for affine restriction
statement:
The restriction isomorphism is the identity for $s=1$, and its two possible
composites on an iterated basic open $D(st)$ agree literally after the
chosen canonical associativity isomorphisms.

proof.text:
On each standard chart, the map for $s=1$ is induced by the identity of the
Rees algebra, hence is the identity. For $s,t$, both composites send a
homogeneous fraction to its image in the localization at $st$; the two
coefficient maps are equal by [lemma-nagata-rees-localization-one]
and [lemma-nagata-rees-localization-mul].
The chart maps therefore agree on a cover, proving the asserted identity
and cocycle equalities globally.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $\varphi\colon A\to B$ and $\psi\colon B\to C$ be ring homomorphisms and
let $I\subseteq A$, $J\subseteq B$, $K\subseteq C$ be ideals with
$J=\varphi(I)B$ and $K=\psi(J)C$, so that $K=(\psi\varphi)(I)C$. Then the
morphisms of [def-nagata-affine-blowup-restriction-map] satisfy

$$
r_{\psi\varphi}=r_\varphi\circ r_\psi\colon
\operatorname{Bl}_K(\operatorname{Spec}C)\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Bl}_I(\operatorname{Spec}A).
$$

proof.text:
Applying $\psi\varphi$ to a coefficient is the same as applying $\varphi$
and then $\psi$, so the graded ring homomorphisms of
[def-nagata-rees-localization-map] satisfy
$\rho_{\psi\varphi}=\rho_\psi\circ\rho_\varphi\colon
\mathcal R_A(I)\to\mathcal R_C(K)$.

The morphism of Proj schemes induced by such a homomorphism $\rho$ is
described chart by chart: for $a\in I$, it maps the standard open
$D_+(\rho(at))$ of the target Proj to $D_+(at)$ by $\operatorname{Spec}$ of
the induced map of degree-zero homogeneous localizations
$\mathcal R_A(I)_{(at),0}\to\mathcal R_C(K)_{(\rho(at)),0}$. Since $K$ is
generated by the image of $I$, the elements $\rho(at)$, $a\in I$, generate an ideal
containing the irrelevant ideal of $\mathcal R_C(K)$, so these standard
opens cover $\operatorname{Bl}_K(\operatorname{Spec}C)$ and the morphism is
everywhere defined. The induced maps of homogeneous localizations are
compatible with composition, so on each standard open
$D_+(\rho_{\psi\varphi}(at))$ the morphisms $r_{\psi\varphi}$ and
$r_\varphi\circ r_\psi$ are $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the same ring map.
As these opens cover $\operatorname{Bl}_K(\operatorname{Spec}C)$, the two
morphisms are equal.
